The tests beside each: askgate.test.ts, new-asks.test.ts, decision-record.test.ts, askgate-report.test.ts.
trickyParts: The breaker's free pass had to stay for the loop it exists to end while no longer covering a different ask, so a rules refusal now records each refused ask's identity (its opening, or the block a retype names) and the breaker branch scans the call's own asks locally, which costs no model call.

goldmark's own footnote parser advances past `]:` alone; it is Dispatch's wrapper (pmdoc's footnoteDefinitionParser.Open) that consumes the label's whitespace, so the scanner mirrors the wrapper and not goldmark.

Sharing the list's bytes had to keep the per-ask 8 KiB ceiling and still list every ask, so an ask needing less than its share hands the remainder on; a call with so many asks that their tags alone exceed the bound lists them all and goes past it, which is stated in the code.

A failed de-duplication read cannot tell a new id-carrying ask from one the stored version holds, so judging only the id-less openers leaves a real gap; it is recorded as ruleAsksPartial rather than hidden, and the report counts it.
deviations: The round-1 fixture dispatch://INFRA-301 was closed at the architect's instruction after the tester released it, so this round's live runs use a new unassigned fixture, dispatch://INFRA-362.
The two items the review left as fast-follow (an empty --dispatch-project, and the record's plugin name) are fixed in this round at the architect's instruction, so the Fast-follow line is none.
No second simplify pass: a round answering a review runs none (skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md).
openQuestions: sjawhar/legion#2159 is still open and this branch carries its commits; the architect watches it and the plan's "when #2159 merges" step runs before the review round that approves the head.
discoveredComplexity: The differential the reviewer built for finding 3 also caught a second kind its own corpus had not reached: before the fix the scanner invented asks in 707 whole-document and 715 fragment comparisons, where a fence opener inside a footnote definition was read as indented code so the fence never opened. Both kinds are zero at this head.

Three of this round's four findings are the same shape — a bound, a counter or a failed read quietly changing which asks are judged — and each was invisible in the entry, which read ruleOutcome "none" either way. The two counts added to the report (asks cut, asks judged in part) are what make that visible to the session that reads Dispatch.
